label: Fix grammar
instruction: Fix spelling, grammar and punctuation. Change nothing else: not the wording, not the tone, not the structure.

label: Rewrite
instruction: Rewrite this so it reads better: say the same thing with different wording and a different sentence structure. Never return the text as it is, however good it already is. Keep the meaning, the voice and roughly the length.

label: Shorten
instruction: Cut this down so it has clearly fewer words than the original, also when it is already short. Keep every point that carries information, drop the rest, and start with a full sentence. Do not add anything.

label: Elaborate
instruction: Expand this with the detail a reader would ask for next. Invent no facts: only draw out what the text already implies.

label: More formal
instruction: Rewrite this in a professional register, with the wording a formal letter uses, so it reads differently from the original. No slang, no contractions, no stiffness either.

label: More casual
instruction: Rewrite this the way you would say it to a colleague, with the wording of everyday talk, so it reads differently from the original. Plain, warm, not sloppy.

label: To bullets
instruction: Turn this into a short bulleted list, one idea per bullet, in the order the text makes them.

label: Translate to EN
instruction: Translate this into English. Match the register of the original. Output the translation only.
